title: Fugaro orchestrator patch
description: One typed change to an orchestrator's state, the only way anything changes it (docs/stateless-orchestrator/spec.md G1). A session or an agent never writes the document: it sends a patch, and the program that applies it decides by the actor's class whether each op may land. This schema is the vocabulary and the shapes; the fence — which class may send what, and what the state it lands on has to be — is code (orchestrator.Apply), and a patch that passes here is still refused there. Like the state document it is closed: a field this release does not model is an error, not something to carry along, because the whole point of a typed op is that a caller cannot smuggle in a change nobody named. Go: internal/orchestrator/patch.go.

base_rev.description: The state revision the patch was built from. A patch built from another one is refused rather than applied on top of a change its author did not see (orchestrator.ErrStaleRev), which is what a caller retries after re-reading.

ops.description: The changes, applied in order. One patch that carries an op the actor may not send changes nothing at all: Apply builds the result on a copy and returns no state when any op is refused.

op.description: One op and the payload its kind takes, and nothing else: the op's kind decides which payload is read, and a payload for another kind is refused rather than ignored (orchestrator.ErrOpPayload).

id.description: The item this op is about. An item that is not there yet is created by this op, and one that is there is changed in the fields the op carries.

spec.description: The plan's folder under docs/ the work belongs to (docs/forge-labels, R3), which becomes the daemon's `spec:<name>` label. Either case is accepted here and stored lower-cased; the class is ASCII and nothing else, so a name that would fold into a passing one — the Kelvin sign into a "k" — is refused as written. A session or a person sets it in the upsert that declares the item, and an upsert that omits it leaves the item's own alone.

external.description: The external ticket this item is, as `github:<owner>/<repo>#<n>` (D2728): the owner and the name lower-case as the installation's own App answers them and GitHub the only host, because it is a dedupe key and two spellings of one ticket would be two items. The ingest builds it and writes it as built — it is checked for shape and never folded. The daemon's alone to write, like the fields below it, and unique across the node's items.

body_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the external ticket's body as it was when the item was ingested, lower-case hex (D2720). The ingest writes it, and it is digested: an item whose issue was edited is not the work a person approved, so the approval is revoked the way any other spec change revokes it.

plan_task.description: The plan node the item is, as `<plan>/<task>` in the shape task.PlanTaskProblem checks (D2704), the same shape and the same bound as the launch record's own field (schemas/task.schema.json). The plan import writes it, and it is part of the spec a person approves: an upsert that changes it revokes a standing approval like any other declaration. Two rules of task.PlanTaskProblem the pattern cannot carry are that a '.' or '..' element and a control character are refused.

adopted.description: Set on an item the daemon wrote for a run already in flight when it took that run's id over (D2702). The daemon's alone to write, and bookkeeping: it says how the item entered the node rather than what the work is, so it moves no digest and the ladder skips every rung that merges for such an item until a person approves it.

phase.description: The daemon's to write, like the fields below it: a patch from a session or a person that carries one of them is refused whole, so an approved item cannot be requeued by whoever is told to carry it out.

intent.description: The declaration of the attempt this launch is for, or how a declared attempt ended. It is here rather than in an op of its own because every intent is written together with the phase, the run id and the attempt number it explains, and one write is what keeps those four consistent.

escalation.description: The ladder's ledger, the daemon's alone to write like the fields above it (G12). The op carries the ledger the item is to have, and Apply refuses anything but an append: the transitions already on the item must be the first ones here, in order, and the rung and the run count only move forward — a transition that happened is not rewritten.

repo.description: The item's repository, which the daemon copies from the item (E12, F27).

run_id.description: The run the block's last move was about, which the daemon copies from the launch or the item.

rung.description: The rung the item is at, and the highest it has entered.

entered_at.description: When it entered that rung: the last transition's own time.

outer_attempts.description: How many of the ladder's own runs the item has spent (orchestrator.MaxOuterAttempts).

transitions.description: The ladder's history, oldest first and append-only (orchestrator.MaxEscalationTransitions).

from.description: The rung the item left. Absent on the first transition, which is an item entering the ladder.

reason.description: Why, as one of escalation.Reasons: a code, never a sentence (G8).

head_sha.description: The head the ladder was looking at, lower-hex and possibly abbreviated.

id.description: The work item and the attempt.

outcome.description: Sent alone, on a later patch, to record how an already declared attempt ended: a declaration carries no outcome, and an outcome alone re-declares nothing.

spec_digest.description: The digest of the spec the person read. Apply refuses it unless it is the item's digest right then, which is what binds the approval to what was approved. There is no approval field on an upsert: an approval comes from this op and from nothing else.

node.description: The node whose items this approves: an imported plan's folder under docs/, as the import wrote it on the items (`spec`), or `backlog` for the standing backlog's node, whose items carry no spec (D2706, D2717, D2735). Apply is handed one node's document, so the node is checked against the items themselves: a listed item tagged with another plan, or a plan's item listed under `backlog`, is not approved by this op.

items.description: The items the import wrote and the digests the person read, which is the whole scope of the approval (D2738). An item whose spec has moved since it was read is skipped rather than approved, and the skip is recorded as one fact naming the item; an id the node does not carry, or one that is not an item of `node`, is skipped silently. Nothing here refuses the patch, so one moved item does not hold up the rest.

digest.description: The digest of the spec the person read, as the import printed it. Apply skips the item unless it is the item's digest right then, which is what binds the approval to what was approved.

outcome.description: How it ended, in a line.

waiting_on.description: The class that has to answer. A decision that waits on a person is closed by a person alone: no session, daemon or decision agent may close it.

answer.description: What was decided. Who decided is the actor's class, not a field here, so a caller cannot claim to be someone else by writing it down.

value.description: What the fact says: empty on a fact_delete, and non-empty on a fact_set, which is how the two branches above read it. A patch that means one and carries the other is refused rather than guessed at.

goal.description: The standing instruction. Only a person may set it.
